list_of_business: Papers to be laid on the Table
Demand for Grants — Fire and Rescue Services

segments.transcript: I present the demands for grants for the Home department. The Kavalan-SOS women's safety app has been re-launched with real-time location sharing to district control rooms. Recruitment of eight thousand additional police personnel is at the final stage. The cyber-crime cell is being expanded to thirty-two district units.

Since this government took office, the number of reported crimes against women has actually risen. The Chief Minister quotes his own department's figures — we ask for independent verification. The Home portfolio should not be held by the Chief Minister himself; it needs a dedicated minister accountable to this House.

The registered increase in crimes against women reflects a real change — more women are choosing to report, because the Kavalan-SOS system has restored their confidence in the police. Conviction data has risen by nine percent. I invite the honourable Leader of the Opposition to inspect the district-level data with me at any time.

Rural police stations remain under-staffed. Stations in Salem, Erode, and the Nilgiris are operating at forty percent of sanctioned strength. Announcements about recruitment must translate to actual postings in the districts, not just Chennai.

The Fire and Rescue Services demand for grants includes forty-six new fire stations, of which thirty-two are in Tier-3 towns. On the honourable AIADMK General Secretary's point on rural policing — the new recruit allocations for Salem and Erode districts have already been notified this morning. The Nilgiris posting will follow within the week.
The House will now adjourn to meet on Monday the 7th of September at 9:30 am after the three-day break.
